correctness.rationale: Under Assumption 2 the admissible product problem splits by interaction component. Detailed balance makes the potential/social ratio of a pair term exactly \(q_iq_j/(q_i+q_j)\), while a player-specific term has ratio \(q_i\). Nonnegative coefficients therefore give \(m_k\mathrm{SC}_k\le\Phi_k\le M_k\mathrm{SC}_k\); minimization and summation prove the bound. Independent positive scaling multiplies both \(M_k\) and \(m_k\) equally and cannot change a component minimizer. The lower bound on every global scaling certificate and the normalization \(c_k=1/M_k\) match, proving the claimed optimum.

value.rationale: The source explicitly admits disconnected vehicle groups. Within that case its global exact-regime coefficient expression can grow without bound under a component rescaling that leaves the selected policy set unchanged. The componentwise theorem removes this gauge dependence, returns a finite intrinsic certificate, and proves the exact best normalization of the source's coefficient method; the improvement can therefore be arbitrarily large rather than a routine constant tweak.
